frequency_question: How often can the federal machinery execute and enact major executive-ordered trade tariffs within 102 days or fewer from initial announcement?
membership_rule: Includes any executive-branch initiated broad sectoral or national-security-based tariff announcements; excludes routine anti-dumping/countervailing duty adjustments managed entirely by administrative agencies without presidential proclamation.

cases.name: Liberation Day Tariffs / Broad Reciprocal Proposals

coverage_note: 3 named; universe of major unilateral presidential tariff actions in modern era is small.
known_gaps: Limited sample size due to infrequency of sweeping unilateral 50 percent tariff threats.
skeleton: Presidential executive orders directing U.S. Customs and Border Protection to alter tariff schedules via Federal Register publication and Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) system updates.
multiplier: 3 total historical major tariff implementation instances examined; 2 successfully completed within a sub-100 day window, 1 delayed or modified.
validity_reason: Valid until the end of the current presidential term governing emergency economic powers and trade procedures.
